title: Purification of astrocyte subtype based on a double reporter mice approach for downstream transcription profiling
protocol: Isolate the animal’s head by decapitation using scissors at the base of the skull.
Drench the fur with 70% ethanol.
Make a small incision in the dorsal skin from the head to the hind limbs to remove the pelt.
Insert small scissors through the abdominal wall muscles and cut laterally to the spinal column in both directions.
Cut the ribs on both sides of the spinal column before removing the viscera connected on its anterior side.
Remove the spinal column by making a transverse cut at the level of the femurs.
Clear the spinal column of soft tissues, cutting it at the level of the last rib which is a landmark of the last thoracic segment.
Keep the cervical and thoracic spinal column for further isolation and remove the lumbar part.
Place the cervico-thoracic column in a petri dish containing cold PBS.
Start cutting the column from one end under a dissecting microscope, peeling off vertebrae with forceps to reveal the spinal cord.
Remove dorsal root ganglion and meninges from the spinal cord explants.
Remove meninges from spinal cord tissue carefully.
Check fluorescence on spinal cord explants to confirm genotyping using a Nikon AZ100 multizoom microscope.
Slice spinal cord into 100 μm sections using a tissue-chopper (Mc Ilwain).
Place each sliced spinal cord in a 35 mm tissue culture dish.
Add 250 μL of DNase solution to the falcon tube containing papain solution.
Add 1 mL of papain/DNase solution per petri dish containing one chopped spinal cord.
Incubate for 60 min at 37°C in a 95%O2:5%CO2 incubator.
Monitor dissociation and adjust timing accordingly to prevent prolonged enzymatic digestion that can affect cell viability.
Gently triturate the mixture by pipetting up and down 10–15 times using a 5 mL pipette.
Centrifuge the dissociated cells at 300 g for 5 min at room temperature.
Mix 2.7 ml of EBSS with 300 μl of ovomucoid solution in a 15 ml falcon tube.
Add 150 μl of DNase solution to the mixture prepared in step 19.
Discard supernatant and resuspend each cell pellet in 500 μL diluted DNase/ovomucoid solution.
Be at the centrifuge as soon as it stops.
Handle 15 mL conical falcon tubes carefully to avoid disturbing the fragile pellet.
Remove the supernatant slowly using a P-1000 pipette, ensuring no pellet is aspirated.
Add 1 mL of ovomucoid in a 15 mL falcon tube and layer the cell suspension on top.
Centrifuge the dissociated cells at 70 g for 6 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 300 μL of PBS + 10% FBS.
Filter the resuspended cells through a 40 μm cell strainer to remove clumps.
Transfer the filtered cells into a 5 mL polypropylene round-bottom tube.
Keep the tube on ice and proceed to sorting as fast as possible.
Run control samples from GFP-reporter mouse, tdTomato-reporter mouse, and wild-type mice to establish gating parameters.
Remove debris and doublets according to FSC-A vs SSC-A plot.
Exclude doublets by gating on FSC-H vs FSC-W.
Further exclude doublets by gating on SSC-H vs SSC-W.
Gate for fluorescence using PE-A vs GFP-A to identify eGFP+ cells.
Identify tdTomato+ cells using the same fluorescence gating approach.
Collect eGFP+/tdT- cell population into a prepared 1.5 mL tube.
Collect eGFP-/tdT+ cell population into a prepared 1.5 mL tube.
Collect eGFP+/tdT+ cell population into a prepared 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 2000g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Process the samples for RNA extraction using standard Trizol reagent with glycogen added as carrier according to manufacturer instructions.
Elute RNA into 35 μL RNase-free water.
Store eluted RNA samples at -80°C for up to 3 months.
Perform library preparation and RNA-Sequencing by Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI, Hong Kong, China) using a BGISEQ-500 RNA-seq platform.
Use FastQC (v0.11.5) to check the quality of each raw fastq file from each sample: two files per sample, one for read1 and one for read2 of the RNA fragment sequenced paired-end.
Use Samtools (v1.9) to process alignment output files in SAM format.
Convert each SAM file into a compressed Binary Alignment Map (BAM) file.
Sort each BAM file following genomic coordinates order.
Generate an index, in BAI format, for each BAM file.
Count the raw number of reads’ pairs aligned on each annotated feature from Ensembl gtf using HT-seq count (v1.0).
Compute for each gene the number of fragments per kilobase million reads (FPKM) using Cufflinks (v2.2.1).
Compute percentage of read pairs aligned and quantified for each sample.
Control the specificity of each sample.
Use STAR to align raw reads on specific sequences, including eGFP and td-Tomato.
Quantify the number of reads for each file on the 2 specific sequences using Samtools idxstat.
Normalize these quantifications by total sequencing depth.
Visualize normalized quantifications into a bar plot.
Import raw datasets in the workspace.
Import the raw pairs count table for each sample.
Check that each table is completely loaded.
Merge all tables into one common data frame with all samples.
Remove rows corresponding to ambiguous or not assigned pairs.
Explore the complete raw dataset.

Check the quality of the count table: proportion of null counts per sample, most expressed genes in each sample, statistical indicator for distribution of reads’ pairs counts for each sample and correlation between each replicate.
Apply Principal Component Analysis on the raw data.
Apply Hierarchical Clustering using Euclidean distance and Ward criterion on the raw data.
Use ggplot2 R-package to draw graphs of PCA results.
Remove genes from the raw count table with an averaged raw read count per sample lower than 1.
Perform Relative Log Expression (RLE) normalization on the cleaned raw counts using DESeq2.
Estimate dispersion parameters for the Negative-Binomial distribution of the data using DESeq2.
Use DESeq2 to apply inferential testing between Olig2-AS and nonOlig2-AS cells.
Apply a Wald test to each gene for differential analysis (DA1).
Correct p values using the Benjamini–Hochberg method for DA1.
Repeat the Wald test and correction for multiple testing for DA2, comparing Olig2-AS with OPC/OL.
Repeat the Wald test and correction for multiple testing for DA3, comparing nonOlig2-AS with OPC/OL.
Find associated gene symbol for each ID using Biomart (v2.48.2).
Convert Mouse ENSEMBL IDs to mouse official gene names using Biomart.
Apply Principal Component Analysis on the normalized data set.
Perform Hierarchical Clustering on the normalized data set using Euclidean distance and Ward criterion.
Compute Pearson correlation between samples.
Plot the correlation results in a heatmap using ggplot::heatmaps.2 R-package (v3.1.1).
Generate plots from DESeq2 output for each differential analysis.
